question.text: One mole of a monoatomic gas is mixed with three moles of a diatomic gas. The molecular specific heat of mixture at constant volume is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><msup><mi>α</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mn>4</mn></mfrac><mi>R</mi><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">J</mi><mo> </mo><mi>mol</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>; then the value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>α</mi></math> will be _____ . (Assume that the given diatomic gas has no vibrational mode.)

solution.text:
Molecular specific heat at constant volume in terms of degrees of freedom is given by CV=f2R

Molecular specific heat of mixture at constant volume is CV/mix=n1CV1+n2CV2n1+n2

=1×3R2+3×5R21+3

=9R4=α24R

⇒α=3
